verdict.winner: Roof repair wins on cost for a young, locally damaged roof; roof replacement wins once age or damage extent crosses the contractor-consensus thresholds.
verdict.reasoning: Roof repair beats replacement when damage stays under 25-30% of the roof area, the roof is under 15 years old, and the deck is sound, because a localized repair costs 5-10x less than full replacement (Home Depot, Kelly Roofing).
verdict.alternate: Roof replacement beats repair when one repair exceeds 50% of replacement cost (the industry '50% rule,' per WeatherShield and Home Depot), the roof passes 20 years (15 on the coast), or three-plus repairs occur in two years (WeatherShield decision rules).

keyFacts: Roof repair runs $360-$1,550 for minor work, per Angi.
An asphalt roof repair averages about $1,174 and typically runs $366-$1,984, per HomeAdvisor.
A NJ leak repair runs $400-$1,000, per HomeAdvisor.
An Essex County roof replacement runs $10,000-$25,000, per HomeAdvisor and Modernize.
A localized repair costs 5-10x less than full replacement, per Home Depot and Kelly Roofing.
Emergency after-hours repair work adds 25-50%, per Integrity Home Exteriors.
Asphalt shingle roofs carry a 20-30-year service life, per InterNACHI.
The '25% rule' (replace when damage exceeds 25% of roof area) is a contractor rule of thumb, per RapidRestore.
The '30% rule' (lean to replace when repair cost approaches 30% of replacement cost) is a contractor rule of thumb, per Josten Roofing, Kellow Construction, and Modernize.
The '50% rule' says replace when one repair exceeds 50% of replacement cost, per WeatherShield and Home Depot.
A roof under 15 years old favors repair; a roof past 20 years (15 on the coast) or with 3-plus repairs in 2 years favors replacement, per the WeatherShield decision rules.
Architectural asphalt loses repair economy faster (around 15-20% of area) because color and weathering match grows harder, per HomeGuide and Modernize.
Asphalt roofs hold most of their 20-30-year design life under 10 years of age, per NAHB.
Actual roof lifespan varies up to plus-or-minus 40% by climate, install quality, and maintenance, per the NRCA.
Older homes report roof leakage at 5.5% versus 3.5% for newer homes (about 2x the rate), per US Census housing-survey data.
Essex County's median home was built in 1981, per housing data, so many original roofs now near end of life.
Roof replacement resets the roof age an insurer depreciates, per NAIC and Triple-I depreciation practice.
Roof insurance pays on an ACV basis (replacement cost minus depreciation) or RCV basis (like-kind cost without that deduction), per NAIC and the Insurance Information Institute.

An RCV policy commonly pays in two stages: a first actual-cash-value payment minus the deductible, then the held recoverable depreciation after the work is completed and invoiced, per the Insurance Information Institute.
In New Jersey only a licensed public adjuster or attorney may negotiate or settle an insurance claim, per N.J.S.A. 17:22B; a contractor cannot waive the deductible or guarantee approval.
A tear-off exposes and repairs the full deck, per ARMA reroofing guidance.
A new asphalt roof recoups about 61% of job cost, per Remodeling/Zonda 2023 Cost vs. Value.
A new roof recoups 60-68% nationally, per Zillow via Opendoor.
A new roof adds about $15,247 to resale value and lets sellers ask 1%-3% more, per Opendoor and Zillow analysis.
Recurring leaks in the same spot signal a systemic failure that a tear-off resolves by exposing and repairing the full deck, per ARMA reroofing guidance.
njContext: An Essex County roof replacement runs $10,000-$25,000, per HomeAdvisor and Modernize.
A NJ leak repair runs $400-$1,000, per HomeAdvisor.

The NJ Uniform Construction Code treats repair or total replacement of the roof covering on a detached 1- or 2-family dwelling as ordinary maintenance, requiring no permit, inspection, or notice, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and the NJ DCA's 2018 alert.

The NJ Uniform Construction Code requires a permit once roof work turns structural (replacing rafters, trusses, or ridge beams) or exceeds 25% of roof area within 12 months on commercial, condo, or attached buildings, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7(b) and 5:23-2.7(c).

The NJ Uniform Construction Code caps a roof at two layers; a recover-over is prohibited once two applications of covering already exist, so a two-layer roof forces a full tear-off replacement, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 and IRC R908.3.1.1.
In New Jersey only a licensed public adjuster or attorney may negotiate or settle an insurance claim, per N.J.S.A. 17:22B.
Essex County's median home was built in 1981, so many original roofs now near their 20-30-year asphalt end of life.

Commercial roof replacement in NJ triggers a UCC permit once roof work exceeds 25% of roof area in 12 months, since the ordinary-maintenance exemption covers only detached 1- and 2-family dwellings, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7(c).
positioning: Position NQR as a registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor (N.J.S.A. 56:8-136), insured, offering a free written inspection and estimate across Essex County. NQR's role on the repair-or-replace call is the inspection and the honest written scope: it photographs the damage, assesses roof age, damage extent, and deck condition, and recommends repair when damage is localized on a sound young roof and replacement when age or damage crosses the contractor-consensus thresholds. On insurance work NQR stays within the contractor role (documenting damage with photos and a written scope) and never negotiates or settles the claim, waives the deductible, or guarantees approval, since N.J.S.A. 17:22B reserves claim negotiation to a licensed public adjuster or attorney. Warranties are framed honestly in two parts: a manufacturer material warranty on the new roofing system plus NQR's own written workmanship warranty on the install, never as manufacturer certification tiers.

buyersGuide.h1: Which Is Better: Roof Repair vs Replacement?
buyersGuide.directAnswerThesis: Repair wins when damage is under 25-30% of the roof area on a sound deck under 15 years old; replacement wins past 20 years, beyond 25-30% damage, or once one repair tops 50% of replacement cost.
